Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a follow-up question at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q2 results. With me on the call are Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer; David Kim, Chief Marketing Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Innovation Officer; and Robert Hayes, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Thompson.

Jamie Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q2, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover eight key aspects: overall financial performance including geographic splits between developed and emerging markets; brand performance tied to A&P spend and ROI; promotional strategies and their effectiveness; organic sales growth guidance for the rest of the year; gross margin performance; key strategic priorities and progress; factors impacting gross margins like commodity costs, pricing, and mix; and new product launches with innovation pipeline updates.

I will now turn the call over to Maria Lopez to provide more detail on our financial results.

Maria Lopez:
Thank you, Jamie. As Jamie mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $15.2 billion, representing a 4% increase as reported and 6% on a constant currency basis compared to the prior year. Organic sales growth—our gold standard metric—was a solid 5%, driven by 3 points from pricing actions and 2 points from volume and mix. Gross margin expanded 170 basis points year-over-year to 48.2%, our sixth straight quarter of gains, bringing the trailing four-quarter average to 47.8%, above our long-term 46-48% target. This was fueled by pricing discipline, mix optimization, productivity savings, partially offsetting input cost pressures. Operating income was strong, and diluted earnings per share came in at $1.42, up 11%. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me dive deeper into some of these elements starting with geographic performance, a critical lens for our resilience and trajectory in the CPG world. We get about 60% of net sales from developed markets—mainly North America and Western Europe—and 40% from emerging markets like Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and parts of Africa and the Middle East. Developed markets posted organic growth of 1%, or 2% excluding FX headwinds, equating to $9.1 billion in sales. North America, 35% of group total, was flat organically on a two-year stack, with 4% pricing offsetting a 3% volume dip as inflation-weary shoppers traded down—Nielsen shows private label up 150 basis points in grocery. But premium plays like our VitalEssence wellness beverages grew 12% in volume, grabbing 1.2 ACV share points in NARTD, ahead of peers. Market share held at 14.5% per IRI, thanks to trade spend tweaks and our AI Shopper Insights Engine boosting promo ROI 18% via local assortment.

Western Europe, 20% of sales, saw 1% organic decline or flat constant currency, hit by energy costs from Ukraine effects pushing COGS up 5%. Volumes fell 2% in beauty like GlowRadiance skincare amid discounter softness, but e-comm hit 22% of sales via Amazon's CPG Accelerator. Sustainability helped—recyclable EcoBrew packaging lifted millennial loyalty 15% per Kantar.

Emerging markets, our growth engine, accelerated to 12% organic on $6.1 billion, third straight double-digit quarter under our Emerging 20/20 initiative with $500 million in local supply and digital GTM. Asia-Pacific led at 15%; China +18% with ZestLife snacks volumes up 10% on urban health indulgences. India 20% via Gramin Boost micro-distribution to 50,000 villages, gaining 2.5 share points on biscuits vs. Parle. Latin America 10% despite FX, TropiFresh up 25% in Mexico on USMCA efficiencies. Africa like Nigeria and South Africa 14%, personal care up 12% on sachets and Digital Van tech lifting sell-out 25%.

This balance shows smart CapEx—65% of $2.5 billion to emerging infra like aseptic lines in Indonesia. Developed margins up 50 bps to 22%, emerging ROIC at 18% vs. 14%. We see developed stabilizing at 2-4% FY24 organic as inflation eases and Power of One bundles reverse volumes; emerging 12-15%, led by China and India.

Shifting to A&P spend and ROI, our marketing engine delivered strongly. FY to date A&P hit levels around 13.2% of sales, up 6% YoY at $1.25 billion full year pace, balanced vs. peers. Q2 saw elevated holiday-like deploys across Nova Crunch snacks, PureGlow skincare, ThirstQuench beverages. Digital now 45% of spend vs. 32% prior, TV/OOH down to 25%, shopper marketing 30%. Blended ROI improved to 2.8x from 2.3x via MMM with Nielsen/Kantar, incrementality tests.

North America 55% of spend, 3.1x ROI on Walmart Connect/Target Roundel scaling 25%, Nova Crunch 4.2x on sponsored search. EMEA 25%, 3.5x on TikTok for PureGlow e-comm GMV up 18%, despite HFSS regs. APAC 15%, top 3.4x with Douyin for ThirstQuench 6x ROAS. LatAm 2.4x optimizing TV to soccer digital.

NovaMix AI on Google Cloud/Snowflake optimizes 70% media real-time with 150M loyalty data, 15% efficiency uplift, 22% CPA drop. Incrementality pilots reallocate $50M from TV to CTV. Sustainability in 20% creatives boosts favorability 7 points. FY24 guide $1.35-1.40B or 13-13.5%, ROI to 3.0-3.2x.

On promotional strategy and effectiveness, trade/consumer promo at $1.2B or 18% sales, flat % but up 7% absolute, 60/30/10 split, 2.8x ROI up from 2.4x, 28% lift per event, 22% of category volume growth in core.

Trade at 3.1x on high-velocity like CrunchTime/RefreshMax, 35% ACV lift at Walmart/Kroger, PromoOptix ML with IRI/ERP forecasting elasticities to -2.8 for CrunchTime, 42% average lift. Consumer digital coupons 45% repeat uplift, 12.5% redemption via app/Ibotta personalization.

North America 120 bps share gain in bevs, Europe 2.3x shifting to health multipacks +1.2% vol vs. category -0.8%, EM 3.5x like Brazil Mercado Libre. Insights: 40% less baseline erosion, omnichannel +22% lift, eco tie-ins +15% ROI. FY24 target 3.0x expanding PromoOptix, blockchain trade.

Gross margins at 48.2% up 170 bps exceeded guide by 70 bps. Price/mix +310 bps: 6.2% AUR global, 85% portfolio priced, NA laundry 9% on pods, beauty trading up. Productivity +240 bps: $450M savings, $120M automation robotic palletizers -15% labor, AI yields -2.2% waste, fixed contracts shielding 12% palm/PET spikes.

Inputs +50 bps headwind milder, sugar/corn down 5-8%, freight +20%. FX +30 bps tailwind. NA 51.4% up 220 bps scale, EMEA 44.2%, APAC/LatAm 42.8%. Power Brands shift divested 12 SKUs, regen ag de-risks 30% inputs. Q3 guide 48.0-48.5%, FY 150-200 bps to 48.5%.

Drilling into margin factors: commodities eased to 4.2% inflation vs. 8.5%, -120 bps gross but -60 net via 75% cocoa hedge at $3,200/MT below $4,500 spot, palm $950, AI sourcing shifts. Pricing 5.8% net or +220 bps, 7.2% list offset 1.4% trade, elasticity -0.35 resilient. Mix +120 bps premium up 14% to 28% sales at 55% margins. Q4 43.5-44.0% guide adjusted for context.

For organic growth guidance, Q3 3-5%, FY24 4-6% assuming stable FX, no M&A, moderating inflation on cocoa/palm/PET still +20% pre-pandemic. Volume/mix +1.5-2.5%: snacks mid-single via VitaPlant bars 2.5 share in plant-based, price/mix +1.5-3% on laundry +2-3%, e-comm 18% higher margin.

NA 4-6% snacks +7% +250 ACV club, EMEA 2-4% bundling, APAC 5-7% China skincare +10%, LatAm 3-5%. RGM AI optimizes 150 bps mix, +400 ACV, $200M ZBB funds $150M brands, 50% PCR packaging unlocks space. Risks cocoa +40%, upside GLP-1 nutrition.

On key strategic priorities under Core4: Portfolio Power—power brands 72% sales +12% organic, divested two laundry for $150M redeploy, VitaGlow +1.2 ACV NA, EcoShield 85% Europe, LatAm NutriBoost 18% Brazil. Innovation—2.8% R&D, 25+ launches, InsightEngine 10B social points, HydraPure Zero $25M velocity, GreenCream +22%, SkinHarmony 30% trial, 25% faster TTM.

Sustainable Leadership—Planet Positive 2030 net-zero, 45% recycled plastic -28% virgin, 35% regen cocoa/palm +12% savings, Indonesia co-ops +18% incomes. Digital Agility—e-comm 22% +500 bps, Amazon 98% ACoS 18%, DTC +35% $180M, AR Europe +22%. Supply resilience—SupplyForge SAP/IoT stockouts 2.1%, turns 7.2x, Mexico nearshoring -30% LT. Q3 EPS $1.42 +11%, ROIC 18.5%, FY 7-9% organic.

(Detailed financial discussion continues with reconciliation to GAAP and segment details.)

Next, David Kim will provide insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.

David Kim:
Thank you, Maria. Our brand building efforts have contributed significantly to our performance, aligning tightly with the A&P and promo strategies Maria outlined. We're seeing strong engagement across channels, especially with our refreshed campaigns leveraging retail media and digital personalization to drive the ROI metrics she shared.

Following David, Lisa Chen will discuss supply chain performance.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you. We continue to optimize our network and deploy advanced tech for efficiency and resilience, tying into the productivity savings and commodity hedges Maria detailed. We're focused on reducing our carbon footprint through regenerative sourcing and nearshoring, supporting margin durability.

After Lisa, Sarah Chen will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you. We're excited about our pipeline of innovative products, building on the launches and trends Maria touched on. Our recent rollout of VitaCrunch Plant-Powered Bars drove 18% of Q3 organic growth, hitting $85 million in nine months with 15% HHP in protein bars per Nielsen, 45,000 ACV, 25% velocity in clubs, 92% repeat intent for $250M run-rate.

Quench+ functional waters in APAC grabbed 22% share in China on Tmall/JD RMB 320M, amid 11% functional CAGR. EcoGlow skincare in Europe €60M on biotech HA and PCR packaging, 30% clean beauty growth. Pipeline robust 120 projects, 35% late-stage: NutriTech microbiome yogurts Q1 US 18% gut scores, SusTech upcycled rice proteins India cereals 10% share, nootropic coffee NA $150M.

Pillars NutriTech/SusTech/DigiSense, agile pods -35% TTM to 18 months, JV Impossible hybrid snacks, EssenVentures 12 startups. New/renos 22-25% FY24 growth, $1.2B incremental.

Finally, Robert Hayes will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.

Robert Hayes:
Thank you. We're focused on expanding distribution and sales execution, leveraging the geographic and channel insights from earlier. E-commerce growth is strong at 22%, with investments in retail partnerships like Walmart and emerging digital in EM driving the ACV gains and velocity.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan.

Emily Carter:
How is your company addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Emily. Sustainability is embedded across our priorities, as Maria noted in strategic progress and margins. Our Planet Positive 2030 targets net-zero Scope 1&2, 100% recyclable packaging, regen ag 50% supply. We've cut virgin plastic 28% to 45% recycled, ahead of peers, resonating with 68% Gen Z per NPS. 35% cocoa/palm regen saves 12% costs, diverted 15,000 tons waste via upcycled platforms. Launches like EcoGlow with GreenScore and PCR, EcoBrew recyclables boosting loyalty 15%. Partnerships in Indonesia boost farmer incomes 18%, and regen soy de-risks climate volatility 1.5% savings. This drives premium pricing +5%, shelf wins at Target/Carrefour, positioning us for sustained growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Michael Patel with Goldman Sachs.

Michael Patel:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Robert Hayes:
Thanks, Michael. Building on Maria's geographic dive, emerging markets are key, sustaining 12-15% growth. Emerging 20/20 $500M invests in local chains, Gramin Boost India 50,000 villages 22% rural ACV +20% growth, China +18% ZestLife, LatAm TropiFresh Mexico +25% USMCA, Africa Digital Van +25% sell-out. CapEx 65% to EM infra like Indonesia/Vietnam aseptic. FY24 12-15% EM, +400 ACV global prioritizing high-velocity like Reliance India, Mercado Libre Brazil, Tencent China. Digital GTM, omnichannel bundling to capture urbanization, health trends.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Jenkins with Morgan Stanley.

Laura Jenkins:
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?

Maria Lopez:
Sure, Laura. Inflation's moderating but sticky, as in our guidance. Pricing contributed +310 bps to margins, 5.8-6.2% net realization resilient elasticity -0.35 vs. -0.45 avg. 7.2% list on staples offset trade 1.4%, premium 9.5% low elasticity -0.15. Demand shows pantry-loading, premiumization in wellness like VitalEssence +12%, but downtrading NA volumes -3% offset pricing. RGM platform optimizes elasticities, EDLP 60% SKUs, subs stabilizing. Guidance embeds no recession pull-forward, cocoa risks but La Nina upside.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays.

David Ruiz:
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?

Lisa Chen:
Excellent point, David. AI is core, as Maria highlighted in productivity. SupplyForge SAP/IoT visibility stockouts to 2.1% from 5.2%, turns 7.2x. PromoOptix ML IRI/ERP elasticities store-level, NovaMix Google/Snowflake real-time media 70% buys 15% efficiency. Shopper Insights Engine +18% promo ROI hyper-local. Yield opt -2.2% beverages, demand forecast SAP Ariba +22% procurement accuracy, shifts origins. Mexico nearshoring -30% LT, robotic palletizers -15% labor Ohio. Blockchain trade DSO -5 days ahead.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Jamie Thompson for closing remarks.

Jamie Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders, backed by the priorities and execution shared today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the GCB Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Geographic performance: developed vs. emerging markets
Organic sales growth guidance for next quarter/year
Factors impacting gross margin: commodity costs, pricing, mix
New product launches and innovation pipeline update

aspect_summary.Geographic performance: developed vs. em: Developed markets (60% sales, $9.1B) achieved 1% organic growth (2% ex-FX), with North America flat and Western Europe 1% decline/flat CC; emerging markets (40%, $6.1B) grew 12% organically, led by APAC (15%, China +18%), India (20%), LatAm (10%), Africa (14%). FY24 outlook: developed 2-4%, emerging 12-15%.
aspect_summary.A&P (advertising & promotion) spend and: A&P spend ~13.2% of sales FYTD (up 6% YoY), $1.35-1.40B FY24 guide; ROI improved to 2.8x from 2.3x (regional highs: NA 3.1x, EMEA 3.5x, APAC 3.4x), targeting 3.0-3.2x FY24 with digital shift to 45% and AI optimization.
aspect_summary.Promotional strategy and effectiveness: Promo spend $1.2B (18% sales, flat % up 7% abs), ROI 2.8x (up from 2.4x), 28% lift/event; trade 3.1x (high-velocity SKUs, 35% ACV lift), consumer digital coupons 45% repeat uplift; FY24 target 3.0x with PromoOptix ML and omnichannel/eco tie-ins.
aspect_summary.Organic sales growth guidance for next q: Q3: 3-5%; FY24: 4-6% (volume/mix +1.5-2.5%, price/mix +1.5-3%), assuming stable FX/no M&A; regional: NA 4-6%, EMEA 2-4%, APAC 5-7%, LatAm 3-5%.
aspect_summary.Gross margin percentage: Q2: 48.2% (+170 bps YoY, 6th straight gain), trailing 4Q avg 47.8% (above 46-48% target); Q3 guide 48.0-48.5%, FY24 +150-200 bps to 48.5%.
aspect_summary.Key strategic priorities and progress: Core4 priorities: Portfolio Power (power brands 72% sales +12% organic, divestitures); Innovation (2.8% R&D, 25+ launches, faster TTM); Sustainable Leadership (Planet Positive 2030: 45% recycled plastic, 35% regen ag, net-zero); Digital Agility (e-comm 22% +500 bps); Supply resilience (stockouts 2.1%, nearshoring).
aspect_summary.Factors impacting gross margin: commodit: Gross margin +170 bps from price/mix +310 bps (6.2% pricing, premium mix +120 bps to 28% sales); productivity +240 bps ($450M savings); inputs +50 bps headwind (commodities inflation eased to 4.2% vs 8.5%, hedges on cocoa/palm); FX +30 bps tailwind.
aspect_summary.New product launches and innovation pipe: Recent launches: VitaCrunch bars ($85M, 15% HHP protein bars), Quench+ (22% share China), EcoGlow (€60M Europe); pipeline 120 projects (35% late-stage: NutriTech yogurts, SusTech cereals, nootropic coffee); new/renos 22-25% FY24 growth, $1.2B incremental; agile pods -35% TTM.
